newsitem.title: USA: USDA to act soon on antitrust report - Glickman.
newsitem.headline: USDA to act soon on antitrust report - Glickman.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman Thursday said USDA would act soon on suggestions by government auditors on how to strengthen the antitrust division that investigates anticompetitive practices in the meat packing industry.
"I do expect you'll see some changes made and announced in the next few weeks," Glickman told reporters before a speech to a women's health group.

A recent report by USDA's Office of Inspector General found the Packers and Stockyards division of the Grain Inspection, Packers and Stockyards Administration was ill-organized to investigate anti-trust violations.
The report said the division needed to be restructured to better mesh economic and investigative staffs and suggested bringing in a manager with antitrust expertise.

Alternatively, the government auditors recommended requesting legislative action to transfer USDA's antitrust responsibilies for probing anticompetive practices to another federal agency such as the Justice Department.

"I would prefer to see if we can beef up these enforcements so to speak internally because I think it might not have the same sense of priorities within the Justice Department in as much as they've got a thousand different things to worry about," Glickman said.

The secretary requested the report as part of USDA's efforts to tackle concentration in the meat packing industry. Within the last five years, 82 percent of all cattle buying nationwide has become concentrated in the hands of only four meat packing companies.
